headlines.text: It was 2021 when the AEW World Tag Team Titles was up for grabs as The Young Bucks vs. Kingston & Moxley went to war, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 8.57 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype. Kingston & Moxley was challenging for gold for the very first time. The Young Bucks was chasing gold for the 10th time. A brawl right from the opening bell, with Moxley memorably chugging a fan's beer mid-fight ? a physical, hard-hitting title defense that saw the champions narrowly hold off two of AEW's toughest brawlers.

It was 2026 when Hazuki made their first appearance under the AEW banner against Maya World, appearing on Collision, rated 7.00 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. Making her AEW in-ring debut against Maya World with her future Owen Hart Cup opponent Persephone watching from commentary, the STARDOM standout Hazuki picked up the win with a Top Rope Senton.

On this day in 2021, Kenny Omega vs. Orange Cassidy vs. PAC went to battle over the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 8.83 ? a match fans still talk about. PAC was challenging for gold for the very first time. A dramatic triple-threat main event story ? the champion resorted to hitting his challengers with all four of his collected titles just to survive, in front of a rabidly pro-Cassidy full-capacity crowd, before finally escaping with a crucifix pin.

secondaries.text: It was 2021 when a new champion was crowned for the AEW Women's World Title as Britt Baker vs. Hikaru Shida battled it out, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 6.45 ? ending the champion's reign at 10 defenses. A passing of the torch after Shida's year-plus reign ? Baker's win capped a long campaign of psychological warfare and physical ambushes, finally toppling the champion via submission to claim the title for the first time.
On a Saturday in 2026, back when Konosuke Takeshita vs. Daniel Garcia clashed for the AEW International Title, appearing on Collision, rated 7.98 ? a good, competitive contest.

Rewind to 2021, when Chris Jericho vs. Jake Hager vs. Ortiz vs. Santana vs. Sammy Guevara vs. Cash Wheeler vs. Dax Harwood vs. MJF vs. Shawn Spears vs. Wardlow settled things in a Stadium Stampede match, headlining the show on Double or Nothing, rated 7.32 ? a good, competitive contest, on an outstanding Double or Nothing '21 show that earned an overall rating of 8.64.
